metadata.source: Kāśinātha Śāstrī Āgāśe: Vācaspatimiśraviracitaṭīkāsaṃvalitavyāsabhāṣyasametāni Pātañjalayogasūtrāṇi, tathā bhojadevaviracitarājamārtaṇḍābhidhavṛttisametāni pātañjalayogasūtrāṇi. sūtrapāṭhasūtravarṇānukramasūcībhyāṃ ca sanāthīkṛtāni ...

body.translated_text: Now, the teaching of <s>yoga</s>. || YS 1.1 ||
<s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of the fluctuations of the mind (<s>citta-vṛtti-nirodha</s>). || YS 1.2 ||
Then the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) abides in its own nature. || YS 1.3 ||
Otherwise, [there is] identification with the fluctuations. || YS 1.4 ||
The fluctuations are fivefold, [either] afflicted or unafflicted. || YS 1.5 ||
[They are] right knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>). || YS 1.6 ||
Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and testimony (<s>āgama</s>) are the [sources of] right knowledge. || YS 1.7 ||
Error is false knowledge not based on the true form [of an object]. || YS 1.8 ||
Conceptualization is [that which] follows verbal knowledge but is devoid of [a corresponding] object. || YS 1.9 ||
Sleep is a fluctuation whose supporting cognition is [that of] absence. || YS 1.10 ||
Memory is the non-deprivation of experienced objects. || YS 1.11 ||
Their cessation [is achieved] by practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). || YS 1.12 ||
Of these, practice is the effort toward steadiness. || YS 1.13 ||
But this becomes firmly grounded when cultivated for a long time, without interruption, and with reverence. || YS 1.14 ||
Dispassion is the consciousness of mastery of one who is free from craving for objects seen or heard about. || YS 1.15 ||
That [dispassion] which is supreme — freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s> — [arises] through knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s>. || YS 1.16 ||
[Cognitive <s>samādhi</s>] is accompanied by deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>), reflection (<s>vicāra</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), and I-am-ness (<s>asmitā</s>). || YS 1.17 ||
The other [<s>samādhi</s>], preceded by the practice of cessation [of all mental activity], has only <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) remaining. || YS 1.18 ||
[This <s>samādhi</s>] arises from worldly existence for the bodiless (<s>videha</s>) and those merged in <s>Prakṛti</s>. || YS 1.19 ||
For others, [it is] preceded by faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). || YS 1.20 ||
[It is] near for those of intense ardor. || YS 1.21 ||
Because of the distinction [in ardor as] mild, moderate, and intense, there is further differentiation even among these. || YS 1.22 ||
Or, through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>. || YS 1.23 ||
<s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s> untouched by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), results (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent impressions (<s>āśaya</s>). || YS 1.24 ||
In him, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed. || YS 1.25 ||
[He is] the teacher even of the ancients, being unlimited by time. || YS 1.26 ||
His designator is the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ). || YS 1.27 ||
Its repetition [should be done] with meditation on its meaning. || YS 1.28 ||
From that, the attainment of inner consciousness and also the absence of obstacles. || YS 1.29 ||
Disease, dullness, doubt, carelessness, laziness, non-abstention, erroneous perception, failure to attain a stage, and instability — these distractions of the mind are the obstacles. || YS 1.30 ||
Pain, despair, trembling of the body, and [irregular] inhalation and exhalation are the companions of distraction. || YS 1.31 ||
For the prevention of these, practice on a single principle [should be done]. || YS 1.32 ||

By cultivating friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) toward those who are happy, suffering, virtuous, and sinful, respectively — [there is] clarification of the mind. || YS 1.33 ||
Or, by exhalation and retention of breath (<s>prāṇa</s>). || YS 1.34 ||

body.text: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī || YS_1.35 ||
body.translated_text: Or, when a higher sensory activity has arisen, it causes steadiness of the mind. || YS 1.35 ||
Or, [a state that is] sorrowless and luminous. || YS 1.36 ||
Or, a mind [directed toward] one free from passion. || YS 1.37 ||
Or, having the knowledge of dream and sleep as its support. || YS 1.38 ||
Or, by meditation on anything one chooses. || YS 1.39 ||
His mastery extends from the smallest atom to the greatest magnitude. || YS 1.40 ||

body.text: kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā samāpattiḥ || YS_1.41 ||
body.translated_text: When the fluctuations have diminished, like a flawless jewel, [the mind] takes on the color of the knower, the knowing, or the known — this is <s>samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption). || YS 1.41 ||

body.text: tatra śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ saṃkīrṇā savitarkā samāpattiḥ || YS_1.42 ||
body.translated_text: There, <s>savitarkā samāpatti</s> is [that which is] mixed with conceptualizations of word, meaning, and knowledge. || YS 1.42 ||
<s>Nirvitarkā</s> [<s>samāpatti</s>] is [that in which], upon purification of memory, [the mind] shines forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own nature. || YS 1.43 ||

body.text: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā || YS_1.44 ||
body.translated_text: By this very [explanation], <s>savicārā</s> and <s>nirvicārā</s> [<s>samāpattis</s>], having subtle objects, are explained. || YS 1.44 ||
And the subtlety of objects extends up to the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). || YS 1.45 ||
These very [<s>samāpattis</s>] are <s>samādhi</s> with seed (<s>sabīja</s>). || YS 1.46 ||
Upon the clarity of <s>nirvicārā</s> [<s>samāpatti</s>], there is inner luminosity. || YS 1.47 ||
There, the wisdom is truth-bearing (<s>ṛtaṃbharā</s>). || YS 1.48 ||
[This wisdom] has a different object from that of scripture and inference, because of [its] particular purpose. || YS 1.49 ||
The impression born of that prevents other impressions. || YS 1.50 ||

body.text: tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ || YS_1.51 ||
body.translated_text: Upon the cessation of even that, through the cessation of all [impressions], seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) <s>samādhi</s> [arises]. || YS 1.51 ||
Austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> constitute <s>kriyā-yoga</s> (the yoga of action). || YS 2.1 ||
[Its purpose is] the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> and the attenuation of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). || YS 2.2 ||
The afflictions are ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), egoism (<s>asmitā</s>), attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and clinging to life (<s>abhiniveśa</s>). || YS 2.3 ||
Ignorance is the field of the others, whether dormant, attenuated, intermittent, or active. || YS 2.4 ||
Ignorance is seeing the permanent in the impermanent, the pure in the impure, happiness in suffering, and the self in the non-self. || YS 2.5 ||
Egoism (<s>asmitā</s>) is the seeming identity of the powers of the seer (<s>dṛg</s>) and seeing (<s>darśana</s>). || YS 2.6 ||
Attachment accompanies pleasure. || YS 2.7 ||
Aversion accompanies pain. || YS 2.8 ||
Clinging to life, flowing on by its own momentum, is firmly established even in the wise. || YS 2.9 ||
These [afflictions] in their subtle [form] are to be overcome by involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>). || YS 2.10 ||
Their modifications are to be overcome by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). || YS 2.11 ||
The storehouse of <s>karma</s>, rooted in the afflictions, is experienced in seen and unseen births. || YS 2.12 ||
As long as the root exists, its ripening [results in] birth, lifespan, and experience. || YS 2.13 ||
These [ripen into] joy or sorrow, depending on whether the cause is virtue or vice. || YS 2.14 ||

body.text: pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhair guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ || YS_2.15 ||
body.translated_text: Because of the suffering caused by change, anxiety, and <s>saṃskāras</s>, and because of the conflict of the <s>guṇas</s>' activities — to the discerning one, all is indeed suffering. || YS 2.15 ||
The suffering yet to come is to be avoided. || YS 2.16 ||
The conjunction of the seer and the seen is the cause of that which is to be avoided. || YS 2.17 ||

The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) has the qualities of luminosity, activity, and stability; it consists of the elements and sense-organs; and its purpose is experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). || YS 2.18 ||
The stages of the <s>guṇas</s> are the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the general (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), the differentiated (<s>liṅgamātra</s>), and the undifferentiated (<s>aliṅga</s>). || YS 2.19 ||
The seer is pure consciousness alone; yet though pure, it perceives through the coloring [of the mind]. || YS 2.20 ||
The very being of the seen is for the sake of that [seer]. || YS 2.21 ||

body.text: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt || YS_2.22 ||
body.translated_text: Though destroyed for one who has attained the purpose, it is not destroyed, because of being common to others. || YS 2.22 ||
Conjunction is the cause of apprehending the nature of the powers of the owned (<s>sva</s>) and the owner (<s>svāmin</s>). || YS 2.23 ||
Its cause is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). || YS 2.24 ||

body.text: tadabhāvāt saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ taddṛśeḥ kaivalyam || YS_2.25 ||
body.translated_text: In its absence, conjunction ceases — this cessation is the liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) of the seer. || YS 2.25 ||
Unwavering discriminative discernment (<s>viveka-khyāti</s>) is the means of avoidance. || YS 2.26 ||
For that [seer], sevenfold is the wisdom [attained] at the final stage. || YS 2.27 ||

body.text: yogāṅgānuṣṭhānād aśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptir ā vivekakhyāteḥ || YS_2.28 ||
body.translated_text: From the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, the light of knowledge [shines forth] up to discriminative discernment. || YS 2.28 ||

Restraint (<s>yama</s>), observance (<s>niyama</s>), posture (<s>āsana</s>), breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), sense-withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) are the eight limbs. || YS 2.29 ||

Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>) are the restraints (<s>yamas</s>). || YS 2.30 ||
[These], not limited by birth, place, time, or circumstance, [constitute] the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>) [when they are] universal. || YS 2.31 ||
Purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> are the observances (<s>niyamas</s>). || YS 2.32 ||
When disturbed by negative thoughts, [one should practice] cultivation of the opposite. || YS 2.33 ||

body.text: vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam || YS_2.34 ||
body.translated_text: Negative thoughts such as violence, whether performed, caused to be performed, or approved of, whether preceded by greed, anger, or delusion, whether mild, moderate, or intense — [the reflection that] they result in endless suffering and ignorance [constitutes] the cultivation of the opposite. || YS 2.34 ||
When non-violence is firmly established, hostility ceases in [the yogi's] presence. || YS 2.35 ||
When truthfulness is firmly established, actions and their fruits become dependable. || YS 2.36 ||
When non-stealing is firmly established, all jewels present themselves. || YS 2.37 ||
When celibacy is firmly established, vigor is obtained. || YS 2.38 ||
When steadfast in non-possessiveness, [there arises] knowledge of the how and wherefore of births. || YS 2.39 ||
From purity, [there arises] disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. || YS 2.40 ||
And [there arise] purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, and fitness for the vision of the self. || YS 2.41 ||
From contentment, unsurpassed happiness is gained. || YS 2.42 ||
From austerity, upon the destruction of impurity, perfection of the body and senses. || YS 2.43 ||
From self-study, union with the chosen deity (<s>iṣṭa-devatā</s>). || YS 2.44 ||
From devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>, perfection of <s>samādhi</s>. || YS 2.45 ||
Posture (<s>āsana</s>) [should be] steady and comfortable. || YS 2.46 ||
[This is attained] by relaxation of effort and absorption in the infinite. || YS 2.47 ||
From that, [one is] not assailed by the pairs of opposites. || YS 2.48 ||

body.text: tasmin sati śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ || YS_2.49 ||
body.translated_text: When that [posture is achieved], <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is the regulation of the flow of inhalation and exhalation. || YS 2.49 ||
[<s>Prāṇāyāma</s>] manifests as external, internal, or restrained [breath], regulated by place, time, and number, [becoming] prolonged and subtle. || YS 2.50 ||
The fourth [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] transcends the domain of external and internal [breath]. || YS 2.51 ||
From that, the covering of light is diminished. || YS 2.52 ||
And fitness of the mind for concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>). || YS 2.53 ||
When the senses withdraw from their own objects, as if imitating the nature of the mind — that is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal). || YS 2.54 ||
From that, supreme mastery over the senses. || YS 2.55 ||
Concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) is the binding of the mind to a [single] place. || YS 3.1 ||
Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is the continuous flow of cognition [directed] there. || YS 3.2 ||

body.text: tad evārthamātranirbhāsaṃ svarūpaśūnyam iva samādhiḥ || YS_3.3 ||
body.translated_text: That very [state], shining forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own nature, is <s>samādhi</s>. || YS 3.3 ||
The three together [constitute] <s>saṃyama</s>. || YS 3.4 ||
From mastery of that [<s>saṃyama</s>], the light of <s>prajñā</s> (higher wisdom). || YS 3.5 ||
Its application is in stages. || YS 3.6 ||
These three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] are inner limbs compared to the preceding [five]. || YS 3.7 ||
Even those are outer limbs with respect to seedless [<s>samādhi</s>]. || YS 3.8 ||

The suppression and emergence of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of emergence and cessation, connected with the mind at the moment of cessation — this is <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of cessation). || YS 3.9 ||
Its peaceful flow [comes] from <s>saṃskāra</s> (repeated practice). || YS 3.10 ||
The decline of all-objectness and the rise of one-pointedness in the mind — this is <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of concentration). || YS 3.11 ||

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ || YS_3.12 ||
body.translated_text: Then again, when the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) are equal — this is <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of one-pointedness) of the mind. || YS 3.12 ||
By this, the transformations of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characteristic), and <s>avasthā</s> (state) in the elements and sense organs are explained. || YS 3.13 ||
The <s>dharmī</s> (substrate) is that which follows the <s>dharmas</s> — whether quiescent, arisen, or indeterminate. || YS 3.14 ||
The difference in sequence is the cause of the difference in transformation. || YS 3.15 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the three transformations, knowledge of the past and future. || YS 3.16 ||

body.text: śabdārthapratyayānām itaretarādhyāsāt saṃkaras tatpravibhāgasaṃyamāt sarvabhūtarutajñānam || YS_3.17 ||
body.translated_text: Due to the mutual superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition, there is confusion; by <s>saṃyama</s> on their distinction, knowledge of the cries of all beings. || YS 3.17 ||
By direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), knowledge of previous births. || YS 3.18 ||
From [<s>saṃyama</s> on another's] <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), knowledge of another's mind. || YS 3.19 ||

body.text: na ca tat sālambanaṃ tasyāviṣayībhūtatvāt || YS_3.20 ||
body.translated_text: But not with its supporting object, because that is not within the scope [of the <s>saṃyama</s>]. || YS 3.20 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, when the power of apprehension is suspended and the connection between the eye and light is broken — invisibility. || YS 3.21 ||

body.text: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamād aparāntajñānam ariṣṭebhyo vā || YS_3.22 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is of two kinds: active and dormant. By <s>saṃyama</s> on that, or from portents — knowledge of death. || YS 3.22 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the others — [corresponding] powers. || YS 3.23 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on powers — the strength of an elephant and so forth. || YS 3.24 ||
By directing the light of higher sensory activity — knowledge of the subtle, the concealed, and the distant. || YS 3.25 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the sun — knowledge of the worlds. || YS 3.26 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the moon — knowledge of the arrangement of the stars. || YS 3.27 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the pole star — knowledge of their movement. || YS 3.28 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the navel center (<s>nābhi-cakra</s>) — knowledge of the arrangement of the body. || YS 3.29 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the throat pit (<s>kaṇṭha-kūpa</s>) — cessation of hunger and thirst. || YS 3.30 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the <s>kūrma-nāḍī</s> (tortoise channel) — steadiness. || YS 3.31 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the light at the crown of the head — vision of the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings). || YS 3.32 ||
Or, from <s>prātibha</s> (spontaneous intuition) — everything. || YS 3.33 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the heart — knowledge of the mind. || YS 3.34 ||

body.text: sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthāt svārthasaṃyamāt puruṣajñānam || YS_3.35 ||
body.translated_text: Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is a cognition that does not distinguish between <s>sattva</s> (intelligence) and <s>puruṣa</s> (pure consciousness), which are utterly distinct. By <s>saṃyama</s> on what exists for its own sake, as distinct from what exists for another — knowledge of <s>puruṣa</s>. || YS 3.35 ||

From that arise <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive), <s>śrāvaṇa</s> (auditory), <s>vedanā</s> (tactile), <s>ādarśa</s> (visual), <s>āsvāda</s> (gustatory), and <s>vārtā</s> (olfactory) [supernatural perceptions]. || YS 3.36 ||

body.text: te samādhāv upasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ || YS_3.37 ||
body.translated_text: These are obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>, but powers in the state of emergence. || YS 3.37 ||

body.text: bandhakāraṇaśaithilyāt pracārasaṃvedanāc ca cittasya paraśarīrāveśaḥ || YS_3.38 ||
body.translated_text: By the loosening of the cause of bondage and by awareness of the passages [of the mind] — entering another's body. || YS 3.38 ||

body.text: udānajayāj jalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣv asaṅga utkrāntiś ca || YS_3.39 ||
body.translated_text: By mastery of <s>udāna</s> (the upward breath) — non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and ascension [at death]. || YS 3.39 ||
By mastery of <s>samāna</s> (the equalizing breath) — blazing radiance. || YS 3.40 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the ear and space — divine hearing. || YS 3.41 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the body and space, and by <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) on the lightness of cotton — passage through space. || YS 3.42 ||

body.text: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ || YS_3.43 ||
body.translated_text: An external, non-imagined mental activity is the <s>mahāvidehā</s> (great disembodied state); from that, the destruction of the veil over illumination. || YS 3.43 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent, and purposive [aspects] — mastery over the elements. || YS 3.44 ||
From that, the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by their properties. || YS 3.45 ||
Beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine firmness — this is perfection of the body. || YS 3.46 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on apprehension, essential nature, <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), inherent connection, and purposiveness — mastery over the sense organs. || YS 3.47 ||

body.text: tato manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaś ca || YS_3.48 ||
body.translated_text: From that, speed of mind, functioning without instruments, and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). || YS 3.48 ||
For one who has merely the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience. || YS 3.49 ||
From <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) even toward that, upon the destruction of the seed of impurity — <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || YS 3.50 ||
When invited by celestial beings, there should be no attachment or pride, for there is the danger of renewed undesirable connection. || YS 3.51 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the moment and its succession — knowledge born of discrimination. || YS 3.52 ||

body.text: jātilakṣaṇadeśair anyatānavacchedāt tulyayos tataḥ pratipattiḥ || YS_3.53 ||
body.translated_text: From that, discernment of two things that are alike, when they cannot be distinguished by class, characteristic, or location. || YS 3.53 ||

body.text: tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam || YS_3.54 ||
body.translated_text: The knowledge born of discrimination is liberating, encompasses all objects, encompasses all conditions, is non-sequential — thus [it is described]. || YS 3.54 ||
When the purity of <s>sattva</s> equals that of <s>puruṣa</s> — <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || YS 3.55 ||
<s>Siddhis</s> (attainments) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity (<s>tapas</s>), or <s>samādhi</s>. || YS 4.1 ||
Transformation into another form of existence [comes] from the overflow of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature). || YS 4.2 ||

body.text: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat || YS_4.3 ||
body.translated_text: The incidental cause does not set the natural forces in motion; it merely removes the obstacles — like a farmer [removing barriers to the flow of water]. || YS 4.3 ||
Created minds arise from <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) alone. || YS 4.4 ||

body.text: pravṛttibhede prayojakaṃ cittam ekam anekeṣām || YS_4.5 ||
body.translated_text: Among the many [created minds], one mind is the director of the diverse activities. || YS 4.5 ||
Of these, that which is born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is free from latent deposits. || YS 4.6 ||
The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogin</s> is neither white nor black; of others, it is threefold. || YS 4.7 ||
From that, the manifestation of only those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that correspond to the fruition of that [<s>karma</s>]. || YS 4.8 ||

body.text: jātideśakālavyavahitānām apy ānantaryaṃ smṛtisaṃskārayor ekarūpatvāt || YS_4.9 ||
body.translated_text: Because <s>smṛti</s> (memory) and <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) are of one form, there is an unbroken continuity even among those separated by birth, place, and time. || YS 4.9 ||
And they are beginningless, because the will to live is eternal. || YS 4.10 ||

body.text: hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṃgṛhītatvād eṣām abhāve tadabhāvaḥ || YS_4.11 ||
body.translated_text: Since they are held together by cause, effect, substratum, and object — in the absence of these, there is the absence of those [<s>vāsanās</s>]. || YS 4.11 ||
The past and future exist in their own form, due to the difference in the paths of the <s>dharmas</s> (properties). || YS 4.12 ||
They are manifest or subtle, and their nature is the <s>guṇas</s>. || YS 4.13 ||
The reality of a thing is due to the unity of transformation. || YS 4.14 ||

body.text: vastusāmye cittabhedāt tayor vibhaktaḥ panthāḥ || YS_4.15 ||
body.translated_text: Even when the object is the same, the paths of mind and object are distinct, due to the difference in minds. || YS 4.15 ||

body.text: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt || YS_4.16 ||
body.translated_text: An object is not dependent on a single mind; for if it were not cognized by that mind, what would it then be? || YS 4.16 ||
An object is known or unknown to the mind depending on whether the mind is colored by it. || YS 4.17 ||

body.text: sadā jñātāś cittavṛttayas tatprabhoḥ puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvāt || YS_4.18 ||
body.translated_text: The modifications of the mind are always known to its lord, <s>puruṣa</s>, because of his changelessness. || YS 4.18 ||
It [the mind] is not self-illuminating, because it is an object of perception. || YS 4.19 ||
And there cannot be cognition of both [the mind as perceiver and as perceived] at the same time. || YS 4.20 ||

body.text: cittāntaradṛśye buddhibuddher atiprasaṅgaḥ smṛtisaṃkaraś ca || YS_4.21 ||
body.translated_text: If one mind were perceived by another, there would be an infinite regress of cognitions of cognitions, and confusion of memory. || YS 4.21 ||
When consciousness (<s>citi</s>), which does not pass from one state to another, assumes the form of that [mind] — there is awareness of one's own cognition. || YS 4.22 ||
The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, [comprehends] all objects. || YS 4.23 ||

body.text: tad asaṃkhyeyavāsanābhiś citram api parārthaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt || YS_4.24 ||
body.translated_text: That [mind], though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s>, acts for the sake of another [<s>puruṣa</s>], because it operates in conjunction. || YS 4.24 ||
For one who sees the distinction [between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>], there is cessation of the cultivation of the notion of self. || YS 4.25 ||
Then the mind, inclined toward discrimination, gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || YS 4.26 ||
In the intervals of that [discriminative knowledge], other <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) arise from <s>saṃskāras</s>. || YS 4.27 ||
Their removal is said to be like that of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || YS 4.28 ||

body.text: prasaṃkhyāne 'py akusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāter dharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ || YS_4.29 ||
body.translated_text: For one who has no self-interest even in the highest meditation, from the constant discernment of discrimination — the <s>dharma-megha samādhi</s> (cloud of dharma concentration). || YS 4.29 ||
From that, the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>. || YS 4.30 ||

body.text: tadā sarvāvaraṇamalāpetasya jñānasyānantyāj jñeyam alpam || YS_4.31 ||
body.translated_text: Then, because of the infinity of knowledge freed from all coverings and impurities, what remains to be known is little. || YS 4.31 ||
From that, the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, having fulfilled their purpose, comes to an end. || YS 4.32 ||
Sequence (<s>krama</s>) is the counterpart of the moment, apprehensible at the end of a transformation. || YS 4.33 ||

body.text: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti || YS_4.34 ||
body.translated_text: The re-absorption of the <s>guṇas</s>, now devoid of purpose for <s>puruṣa</s> — this is <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom), the establishment in one's own nature, or the power of pure consciousness. || YS 4.34 ||
